diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a given vector $\bmx$, define $\bmx_{1/2}:=\frac{1}{2}\hx+\frac{1}{2}\bmx$ and $\bmx_{1/4}:=\frac{1}{4}\hx+\frac{3}{4}\bmx$.
For the case $\alpha\in\big[\frac{1}{2},1\big)$, analogous to the proof of Theorem \ref{thm_KMaccel}, we can establish the following result.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis of Theorem thm_KMaccel1 refers to $\hx_{1/2}$, a symbol never defined in the source; the only subscripted points defined are $\bmx_{1/2}:=\frac{1}{2}\hx+\frac{1}{2}\bmx$ and $\bmx_{1/4}$. Under the source's own subscript convention, $\hx_{1/2}$ would denote $\hx$ itself, in which case the hypothesis $T\bmx\in O(\hx,\|\bmx-\hx\|)$ holds for every $\bmx$ by nonexpansiveness, while the conclusion $\theta^*\geq0$ is false: for $T=\frac{1}{4}\mI+\frac{3}{4}R$ with $R$ the rotation by 120 degrees in $\mathbb{R}^2$ ($\frac{3}{4}$-averaged with unique fixed point $0$), one gets $\theta^*=-\frac{1}{3}<0$ for every $\bmx\neq0$. In addition, no proof is supplied: the proof of Theorem thm_KMaccel only yields $\theta^*\geq\frac{1}{2\alpha}-1$, which carries no sign information for $\alpha\in[\frac{1}{2},1)$, so the asserted 'analogous' argument does not establish the sign claims. Under the natural reading of $\hx_{1/2}$ as the midpoint $\bmx_{1/2}$, the statement is true.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\hx_{1/2}$ by the defined midpoint $\bmx_{1/2}=\frac{1}{2}\hx+\frac{1}{2}\bmx$ and add the missing argument: $\theta^*\geq0$ iff $\langle\bmx-T\bmx,\hx-T\bmx\rangle\leq0$ iff $T\bmx$ lies in the closed ball with diameter $[\bmx,\hx]$ (Thales), then repeat the Pythagorean computation from the proof of Theorem thm_KMaccel.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm_KMaccel1 is ill-defined as written (and false under the literal reading of the source's subscript convention) and unproven. It is used only motivationally before the definition of TKMA, so no downstream formal result or algorithm guarantee is invalidated.
issues.title: Theorem thm_KMaccel1: hypothesis uses the undefined point hx_{1/2} and no proof is given
issues.why_classification: The intended statement is true and provable by a short local argument; repairing the notation and supplying the elementary proof preserves every substantive claim and guarantee, and nothing downstream depends on this theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: According to \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}, the complete iterative scheme of the TKMA for solving model \eqref{TVdenoise} is given as follows.
Let $T$ be an $\alpha$-averaged nonexpansive operator, where $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$, and let $\{\bmx^k\}$ be a sequence generated by \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}.
For the `Cameraman' image, the parameters $\mu$ and $\lambda$ are set to $10$ and $0.999/4$, respectively.

This experimentally verifies that the condition $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|<+\infty$ in Theorem \ref{convergerate} is satisfied in the denoising scenario, thereby ensuring the convergence rate of TKMA as established by the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Every convergence result for TKMA (Lemma lem:monotonic, Theorems thm:conv and convergerate) requires $T$ to be $\alpha$-averaged with $\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{2}]$, i.e. firmly nonexpansive. The paper justifies the denoising instantiation only by the fact that $T_2$ is 'averaged nonexpansive when $\lambda<\frac{1}{4}$'. But $T_2=(\mI-\prox_{\frac{1}{\lambda}\phi})\circ\mA$ composes the $\frac{1}{2}$-averaged operator $\mI-\prox_{\frac{1}{\lambda}\phi}$ with the affine map $\mA(\bmy)=\bmB\bmx+(\mI-\lambda\bmB\bmB^{\top})\bmy$; the composition's averaging constant is $\frac{1}{2-\beta}$ with $\beta=\lambda\mu_{\max}(\bmB\bmB^{\top})/2$, which exceeds $\frac{1}{2}$ for every $\lambda>0$, so the stated fact does not meet the theorems' hypothesis. For the value actually used, $\lambda=0.999/4$ (both Cameraman and Lighthouse; $\mu_{\max}(\bmB^{\top}\bmB)\leq8$ and is close to 8 for the first-order difference matrix $\bmB$ defined in the source, so $\lambda\mu_{\max}\approx2>1$), $T_2$ is not even monotone: on the nonempty region where $\mA(\bmy)$ lies componentwise inside the clipping range of $\mI-\prox_{\frac{1}{\lambda}\phi}$ (with $\phi=\mu\|\cdot\|_1$ this operator is a componentwise clip), $T_2$ coincides with the affine map $\mA$, whose linear part $\mI-\lambda\bmB\bmB^{\top}$ has eigenvalues $1-\lambda\mu<0$; taking $\bmx-\bmy$ along an eigenvector with $\mu>1/\lambda$ gives $\langle T_2\bmx-T_2\bmy,\bmx-\bmy\rangle<0$. Hence $T_2$ is not $\alpha$-averaged for any $\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}$, the hypotheses of thm:conv and convergerate cannot hold for the denoising experiments, and the claim that the numerics 'ensur[e] the convergence rate of TKMA as established by the theorem' is unsupported (a finite plot also cannot verify the infinite-series hypothesis $\sum|\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|<\infty$).

failure_location.quote: Thus operator $T_2$ defined by \eqref{operatorTfordenoising} is averaged nonexpansive when $\lambda<\frac{1}{4}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either establish convergence (and the rate) of TKMA for the operator $T_2$, which lies outside the $\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}$ class whenever $\lambda\mu_{\max}(\bmB\bmB^{\top})>1$ (in particular at the $\lambda$ used) and would require new analysis beyond the present proofs, or explicitly withdraw the convergence/rate guarantees and the 'theoretically guaranteed' claim for the denoising application.
issues.overall_effect: The 'TKMA for TV denoising' procedure and both denoising experiments ($\lambda=0.999/4$) have no established convergence or $o(1/\sqrt{k})$ rate guarantee; the paper's 'theoretically guaranteed' framing for image denoising, contribution (iii), and the claim that Theorem convergerate's rate is ensured in the denoising scenario are unsupported. The formal theorems thm:conv and convergerate themselves remain valid as stated for $\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{2}]$.
issues.title: TKMA for TV denoising has no established convergence guarantee: T_2 is not alpha-averaged for any alpha<=1/2
issues.why_classification: The required hypothesis (firm nonexpansiveness) is provably violated at the experimental $\lambda=0.999/4$ and is established for no $\lambda$ in the source; every resolution either excludes this advertised application from all guarantees or requires essentially new convergence analysis outside the $\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2}$ framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Based on \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}, the TKMA for solving model \eqref{lowmatrix} can be given as follows.
Let $T$ be an $\alpha$-averaged nonexpansive operator, where $\alpha\in(0,1/2]$, and let $\{\bmx^k\}$ be a sequence generated by \eqref{eq:IKMAiter}.
We define $f(\bmX):=\frac{1}{2}\|P_{\Omega}(\bmX-\bmA)\|^2_F$, and denote by $P_{\mathcal{C}}$ the projection operator onto the set $\mathcal{C}$.
The step size parameter $\alpha$ is set to $1.99$.
In this work, we propose a more efficient and theoretically guaranteed fixed-point type algorithm, Two-step KM Algorithm (TKMA).

issues.failure_explanation:
Theorems thm:conv and convergerate require $T$ to be $\alpha$-averaged with $\alpha\in(0, rac{1}{2}]$ (firmly nonexpansive). The operator $T_3=P_{\mathcal{C}}(\mI-\alpha
abla f)$ composes the $ rac{1}{2}$-averaged projection $P_{\mathcal{C}}$ with the $ rac{\alpha L}{2}$-averaged gradient step $\mI-\alpha
abla f$, so its averaging constant is $ rac{2}{4-\alpha L}> rac{1}{2}$ for every admissible step $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$; the offered justification ('averaged nonexpansive when $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$') therefore does not meet the theorems' hypothesis. For the step actually used, $\alpha=1.99$ with $L=1$ (since $
abla f=P_{\Omega}( mX- mA)$ is 1-Lipschitz for $f( mX)= rac{1}{2}\|P_{\Omega}( mX- mA)\|_F^2$), $T_3$ is not even monotone: near any point whose gradient step lands in the interior of the nuclear-norm ball (where $P_{\mathcal{C}}$ acts as the identity), $T_3$ is affine with linear part $\mI-1.99P_{\Omega}$, whose eigenvalue on $\Omega$-supported directions is $1-1.99=-0.99<0$. Hence $T_3$ is not $\alpha$-averaged for any $\alpha\leq rac{1}{2}$, and the paper's convergence and rate guarantees do not apply to the matrix-completion experiments.

failure_location.quote: It is easy to see that this operator is averaged nonexpansive when $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$, where $L$ is the Lipschitz constant of $\nabla f$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either prove convergence of TKMA for $T_3$ — whose averaging constant exceeds $\frac{1}{2}$ for every step $\alpha\in(0,2/L)$ and which is provably not firmly nonexpansive for $\alpha>1$ (including the $1.99$ used) — requiring analysis beyond the present proofs, or withdraw the convergence/rate guarantee claims for the matrix-completion application.
issues.overall_effect: The 'TKMA for Low-rank Matrix Completion' procedure and both experiments (rank 30 and rank 50, $\alpha=1.99$) have no established convergence or rate guarantee; the paper's claims of a 'theoretically guaranteed' algorithm applied to low-rank matrix completion (contribution (iii), abstract) are unsupported for this application. The formal theorems remain valid for $\alpha\in(0,\frac{1}{2}]$.
issues.title: TKMA for low-rank matrix completion has no established convergence guarantee: T_3 is not alpha-averaged for any alpha<=1/2
issues.why_classification: The required hypothesis is provably violated at the step size used ($T_3$ is not even monotone) and the averaging constant exceeds $\frac{1}{2}$ for every admissible step; no comparable guaranteed version of the application claim survives without essentially new convergence analysis.
